title: Open Checklist Field Report
description: A structured report against a checklist file: this item is stale, this does not match my aircraft, this was transcribed wrong, a newer source revision exists. Structured rather than free-text because a comment thread cannot demote a file's verification state and a report can. This is the mechanism that makes a community-maintained corpus more current than a PDF library rather than merely as current.

target.description: What the report is about. content_hash pins the exact version the reporter was looking at, which is what makes a report resolvable months later: without it, 'item 4 is wrong' becomes unanswerable as soon as the file changes.

type.description: transcription_error = the file does not match the source it claims. stale_item = the file matches its source, but the source has been superseded. source_revision_available = a newer revision of the source document exists. airframe_variation = correct for the type but wrong for a particular aircraft. procedural_concern = the procedure as written looks unsafe or unworkable. rights_concern = the rights or provenance claim looks wrong. improvement = wording, ordering or completeness, no defect alleged.

severity.description: Reporter's assessment. Not authoritative; a maintainer sets the confirmed severity on resolution.

relationship.description: How the reporter comes to know. An owner or mechanic reporting on their own aircraft carries different weight from an anonymous reader, and the format should let a maintainer see which they are.

as_written.description: What the file currently says, quoted. Lets a maintainer confirm the reporter was looking at what they think they were.

evidence.description: Why the reporter believes it. A report with no evidence is still worth filing, but it cannot by itself justify changing a safety document, and the absence should be visible rather than inferred.

status.description: open = filed, not yet assessed. confirmed = a maintainer agrees. rejected = assessed and not accepted. fixed = the file has been changed. duplicate = already reported. cannot_reproduce = the claim could not be checked against the source.

resolution.description: Required once status leaves 'open'. A report closed with no stated reason is how a corpus quietly accumulates unaddressed safety claims.

demoted_verification.description: True when confirming this report reduced the file's verification state. Expected for a confirmed transcription_error or stale_item on a previously reviewed file: a review of content now known to be wrong no longer means anything.

allOf.comment: Anything other than an open report must say how it was resolved and by whom.
A duplicate has to name what it duplicates, or the pointer is useless.
A staleness claim rests on something having superseded the source, so it must identify what.
An alleged transcription error must quote what the file says, so it can be checked without guessing which line is meant.
A report about a specific aircraft should identify it.
